title: Computational thinking
terms: Removing unnecessary detail while retaining what is important to a problem.
Representing data through an appropriate interface or model.
Breaking a complex problem into manageable smaller problems.
Anticipating inputs, outputs, constraints and consequences.
Organising a solution into a clear sequence of steps.
Using evidence, conditions and rules to draw valid conclusions.
Condition that must be true before an algorithm or operation starts.
A simplified representation used to reason about a real system.

title: Thinking concurrently
terms: Multiple tasks make progress over an overlapping time period.
Tasks execute at the same time on separate processing resources.
Outcome varies depending on the timing or ordering of operations.
Code accessing shared state that requires controlled entry.
Ensuring only one task accesses a protected resource at a time.
Two or more tasks remain blocked waiting for resources held by others.
Coordinating tasks so shared state remains consistent.

title: Global and local scope
terms: The region of a program in which an identifier can be used.
Variable accessible within its declared subroutine or block.
Variable declared outside local routines, available across a wider scope.
The period during execution for which a value or variable exists.
A local identifier hides another identifier with the same name.
A named input received by a subroutine.

title: Subroutines, parameters and files
terms: Named subroutine that performs a task without returning a function value.
Subroutine that returns a value to its caller.
Parameter named in a subroutine's definition.
Value or variable supplied when a subroutine is called.
Passing access to a variable so a subroutine can modify the caller's value.
Organising a program into separate, purposeful components.
Opening, reading, writing and closing persistent files.

title: Debugging with an IDE
terms: A location where a debugger pauses execution for inspection.
Run a statement and enter a called subroutine.
Run a statement without stepping through a called subroutine.
IDE display that tracks expressions or variable values during execution.
Code that violates the programming language's grammatical rules.
Code runs but produces an incorrect result.
Failure encountered while a program is executing.

title: Object-oriented programming
terms: Blueprint defining attributes and methods for a kind of object.
An instance of a class with its own state.
Special routine used to initialise a new object.
Combining data and methods and controlling access to state.
Deriving a class from another to reuse and extend behaviour.
Using a shared interface with behaviour that depends on the object.
Providing a derived-class implementation of an inherited method.

title: Data structure algorithms
terms: Last In, First Out: the most recent stack item is removed first.
First In, First Out: the earliest queued item is removed first.
Operations that add and remove items at the top of a stack.
Operations that add at a queue's rear and remove at its front.
A fixed-size queue whose indices wrap around when necessary.
Tree ordered so smaller keys appear left and larger keys right.
Visiting nodes or vertices in a defined sequence.
Graph representation storing neighbouring vertices for each vertex.

title: Searching and sorting
terms: Checks entries sequentially until a target is found or the list ends.
Repeatedly halves a sorted search range.
Builds a sorted prefix by inserting each next value.
Divides a list and merges sorted portions.
Partitions around a pivot and sorts the partitions.
How algorithmic work grows as input size increases.
Binary search requires the input range to be ordered.
